title: Claude Messages API cheatsheet
sub: Supplementary reading - Domains 1, 2, 5 and part of 4

blocks.md: One turn is: you send a request, Claude writes one reply and a stop_reason, and your code decides what happens next.
Every box in a diagram and every table row has an ID. Later sections point back to them.

rows: Rules for sending results back, and for subagents

blocks.alt: diagram A: one conversation turn and the loop, steps A1 to A6

blocks.md: diagram A: one conversation turn and the loop, steps A1 to A6
Claude writes one reply per call. Everything else, including the loop, is your code. Where each step is explained:

items: A1 sends the request: fields C1 to C19.
A2 returns the reply: fields D1 to D8, blocks K1 to K8.
A3 reads `stop_reason`: values B1 to B7.
A5 and A6 run when `stop_reason` is `tool_use` (B3): rules T1 to T13. Then you call again. A subagent is started the same way (T14, T15).

blocks.alt: request fields C1 to C19 in six groups

blocks.md: request fields C1 to C19 in six groups
A1 sends these fields. Three are required: `model` (C1), `max_tokens` (C2) and `messages` (C3). Everything else shapes the reply. Each row below carries the same ID as its box above.

rows: Use the exact model ID from the docs
Hitting it gives `max_tokens` (B5). Thinking tokens count toward it. Setting it to 0 only warms the prompt cache and returns no reply
The chat so far, alternating `user` and `assistant` turns

No `system` role exists. Up to 100,000 messages per request. Consecutive turns with the same role are combined. A final `assistant` message is a prefill: models that don't support it return a 400. You resend the whole history every call
Standing instructions such as goal or role
A top-level field, not a message. Resend it every call
Names, descriptions and schemas cost input tokens. `strict: true` enforces the schema. When continuing (A6), keep the same array: omitting a tool's definition gives a 400
`disable_parallel_tool_use` goes inside it. Not verified: which models allow `any` or `tool` with extended thinking. Check your model
Type `adaptive`, or type `enabled` with a `budget_tokens` of at least 1,024. Accepted types depend on the model. Adds `thinking` blocks (K2)
Custom text that makes Claude stop
A match gives `stop_sequence` (B2), and the `stop_sequence` field (D4) names it
Send the reply as server-sent events
Output options such as effort and format

Cache token counts show up in `usage` (D6)
Pass back the ID from the last response (D7) or earlier files are lost

blocks.md: response fields D1 to D8 and content blocks K1 to K8
A2 returns these fields. Every successful response carries them. Errors (4xx and 5xx) are separate and mean the request failed. Rows below use the box IDs: D for fields, K for content blocks.

rows: A list of blocks, see K1 to K8
Loop over every block. Never assume `content[0]` is the text
Present on every successful response. Branch on it every time (A3, B1 to B7). While streaming it is `null` in `message_start`
`null` for every other stop reason. `category` may be null. `explanation` is for display only: don't parse it
Total input = `input_tokens` + `cache_creation_input_tokens` + `cache_read_input_tokens`. `output_tokens` is above zero even for an empty reply. Final figures arrive in `message_delta` when streaming
Send its ID back when you continue (C13)

blocks.md: The `content` list (D2) can hold these block types.

rows: Only when extended thinking is on (C7)
Reasoning you cannot read. Details not checked here
Has `id`, `name`, `input`. Answer it with a `tool_result` that has the same ID (A5, A6)
Its result block (K7) comes back in the same response, unless the call is unfinished (see B3)
Check each block's `id` for a matching result block
Marks the point where a server-side fallback happened (B7)

blocks.md: Seven values exist today. A stop reason is a normal HTTP 200, not an error. Write a branch for each one, plus a catch-all that logs unknown values, because the list has grown before.

blocks.alt: 7 stop_reason values in 3 groups, with the action for each

blocks.md: 7 stop_reason values in 3 groups, with the action for each
Green means show the answer. Blue means call the API again. Amber means the reply is cut short or refused: handle it, never show it as complete. The table below carries the edge cases.

rows: Can be empty (2 to 3 tokens). Causes: text added right after `tool_result` blocks, or sending Claude's finished reply back with nothing new. Don't retry it unchanged. Last resort: add a new user message such as "Please continue"
Claude produced one of your stop markers (C8)
The field is `null` for every other reason
Claude asks you to run client tools
Run them and return `tool_result` blocks (A5, A6, T1 to T13)

May also hold a `server_tool_use` block with no result yet (a server tool and a client tool in one parallel group). Then send only the client results, keep the same `tools` array, and add no text after them. Code-execution calls carry a `caller` field: send results back and pass the `container` ID
A server-tool loop hit its limit (default 10 per request)
If the response has a `container`, send its ID next time or earlier files are lost. Never used while your own client tool is waiting: that is always `tool_use`
Raise the limit, or continue the reply

If it ends in a `tool_use` block the input is incomplete: retry with a higher limit. To continue text, resend the partial reply as an `assistant` message plus "Please continue from where you left off"
The reply filled the model's context window

Lets you ask for a large `max_tokens` without counting input. On by default from Sonnet 4.5. Older models need beta header `model-context-window-exceeded-2025-08-26`. SDKs type it in the beta namespace
Read `stop_details` (D5), discard the partial output, retry on a different model

Arrives as HTTP 200. `stop_details` has `type`, `category` (cyber, bio, frontier_llm, reasoning_extraction, general_harms, or null), `explanation` and `recommended_model`. Billing differs by category. Fallback options: server-side (beta header `server-side-fallback-2026-07-01`, `fallbacks` parameter, up to 3 models, not on the Batches API), SDK middleware, or a manual retry. Haiku 5.5 has no server-side fallback. Branch on `stop_reason`, not on `category`

blocks.md: While streaming, `stop_reason` is `null` in `message_start` and appears only in `message_delta`.
Tools differ mainly by where the code runs. Claude never executes anything itself: for your tools it only asks.

rows: Your own functions, plus Anthropic-defined `bash`, `text_editor`, `computer`. In the Agent SDK and Claude Code, also the subagent tool `Task` (now named `Agent`)
The results, with nothing for you to handle (K5, K7)
Run the call and send a `tool_result`. For `Task`, that means starting the subagent and returning its result
Nothing, unless a server tool shares a parallel group with a client tool, or you get `pause_turn` (B4)

blocks.md: Rules for sending results back.

rows: Send Claude's reply back unchanged, then a user message with the results
`tool_use_id` in each result must equal the `id` of its `tool_use` block

`tool_result` blocks must come immediately after their `tool_use` blocks, with no message in between. Breaking this gives the error "tool_use ids were found without tool_result blocks immediately after"
With parallel calls, put every `tool_result` in a single user message. Separate messages teach Claude to avoid parallel calls
`tool_result` blocks come first in that message, any text after. With a server tool in the group, add no text after the results: that gives a 400
Still return a result, with `is_error: true` and a message that tells Claude what went wrong and what to try. Claude retries invalid calls 2 to 3 times
`content` can be a string, or text, image, document or search_result blocks
On by default. Turn off with `disable_parallel_tool_use: true` inside `tool_choice`
Claude may omit required parameters. `strict: true` on a custom tool forces your schema
Keep untrusted content inside `tool_result` blocks, not in `system` or plain user text
Tool definitions count as input tokens. Server tools can add usage charges, such as per search
The SDK tool runner handles the loop, result formatting and retries for you

In the Agent SDK and Claude Code, Claude spawns a subagent by calling a tool. It was renamed from `Task` to `Agent` in Claude Code v2.1.63. Current SDKs emit `Agent` in `tool_use` blocks but still use `Task` in the `system:init` tools list and in `permission_denials`, so check for both names. Put it in `allowedTools` so calls are approved without a prompt. Exam guides call it required for a coordinator to spawn subagents

A subagent starts with a fresh context window and no parent conversation. The only channel from parent to subagent is the tool's prompt string, so put file paths, errors and decisions in it. Messages from inside a subagent carry a `parent_tool_use_id`

blocks.md: Set `stream: true` and the reply arrives as events in this order. The loop is unchanged: you just wait for the end of the stream before acting.

rows: One per block. Some blocks arrive whole in one event
Many per block. Tool JSON arrives in fragments. By default it is buffered; `eager_input_streaming` lowers latency
Parse the tool JSON now, not earlier
The only place `stop_reason` appears. There can be one or more of these
There is no `[DONE]` marker. SDK helpers such as `get_final_message()` collect the final message for you
Can arrive anywhere. An error can come in-stream after an HTTP 200 (`overloaded_error` matches 529). Handle unknown event types instead of failing
Claude 4.5 and earlier: put the partial text in an `assistant` message. Claude 4.6 and later: put it in a `user` message. Tool use and thinking blocks can't be partially recovered

blocks.text: Ten rules to memorise, mapped to the exam

blocks.md: The exam is Claude Certified Architect, Foundations. Facts about it here come from two third-party summaries, not the official guide, so check them: 60 scenario-based questions, 120 minutes, closed book, pass mark 720 of 1000. Five domains: D1 Agentic Architecture and Orchestration (27%), D2 Tool Design and MCP Integration (18%), D3 Claude Code Configuration and Workflows (20%), D4 Prompt Engineering and Structured Output (20%), D5 Context Management and Reliability (15%). The domain tags below are my own mapping. This sheet covers D1, D2, D5 and part of D4. It does not cover D3.

rows: Drive the loop from `stop_reason`: continue on `tool_use`, stop on `end_turn`. Don't parse the reply text to guess if it is done. Don't use an iteration cap as the main stop condition
Claude only asks for tools. Your code runs them. Spawning a subagent is also a tool call (`Task`, now `Agent`), and the subagent sees only the prompt you pass it
The API remembers nothing: resend `system`, `tools` and `messages` every call. Put facts that must survive in a block you always resend
Enforce business rules in code, not in the prompt. A prompt is advice. Code is a guarantee
On `tool_use`: echo Claude's reply, then send all `tool_result` blocks in one user message, results first, IDs matching
If a tool fails or is skipped, still return a `tool_result` with `is_error: true` and a message Claude can act on
Give each tool a clear description, keep the tool list short, and use `tool_choice` or `strict: true` when the output must follow a schema
On `pause_turn`: send the reply back unchanged, with the `container` ID if there is one
`max_tokens` and `model_context_window_exceeded` mean truncated: never show them as complete. `refusal` is HTTP 200: read `stop_details`, discard the partial output, use a fallback model
When streaming, parse tool JSON only after `content_block_stop`. `stop_reason` arrives only in `message_delta`
API detail, little exam weight (my judgement)

blocks.md: One conflict with my earlier advice: I told you to cap loop rounds. R1 says the stop condition is `stop_reason`, and exam sources describe a round cap as the wrong primary stop. A cap as a backstop against runaway loops is still sensible engineering. Treat it as a safety net, never as the way the loop ends.

items: The official exam guide was not read. Exam facts, domain weights and my domain tags come from third-party summaries.
Which newest models reject forced `tool_choice`, and whether `any` or `tool` work with extended thinking. Two doc snippets disagree. Check your model.
`output_config`, `speed`, `inference_geo`, the ID headers and `redacted_thinking`: named in the reference, details not checked.
`temperature`, `top_p`, `top_k` are absent from the current reference page. I could not confirm they are accepted by every model.
Two points are my own advice, not doc rules: use a round cap only as a backstop, and don't put secrets in `system`.
